title: Module builder: author a form with sample pre-fill + Health Canada review
walkthrough:
You start on "Your product dossiers", a grid of dossier tiles under a top bar. Clicking "New dossier +" opens a card with two fields, "Dossier ID" and "Product name". You must know Health Canada's ID format up front: entering anything else shows the error "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)". If you don't have one, a small link offers "No ID yet? Start with a placeholder →", which fills a d-prefixed draft ID. Pressing "Create & open →" drops you into the Module 1 workspace.

The workspace is three columns. The top bar shows module tabs M1–M5 plus chips for "Application Viewer", "Audit", "Portfolio", and "Journey". The left rail is a section tree: each row has a status glyph, the section number, title, and a badge reading "req" or "opt"; AI-capable sections add a "✦AI" badge. Sections that don't apply collapse under "Not required for this generic". The right rail shows module progress ("required sections complete") and three gate flags: "Documents", "Fee", "Valid eCTD".

Selecting a section opens the center panel: an eyebrow line ("Module 1 · Section …"), the section title, and a guidance box headed "What Health Canada needs here" with format notes and a "Health Canada guidance ↗" link. Below sits an action bar with tabs "⬆ Upload", "✦ Author in-app", and sometimes "⊘ Mark N/A".

Choosing "✦ Author in-app" on an AI-draftable section first shows a mode toggle: "💬 Draft with AI" or "✦ Sample & edit". The sample-and-edit form loads pre-filled, with the note "Pre-filled with a realistic sample from your dossier — edit every field to your product, then author. Fields marked sample are worked examples to replace." Fields like "Canadian Reference Product (brand)", "BE study design", and "AUC 90% CI" carry a small "sample" tag. Two buttons follow: a primary "Author" button naming the section (showing "Authoring…" while busy) and a secondary "Review vs Health Canada".

Authoring attaches a document above the form, listed with file size, a truncated md5 checksum, an "authored in-app" provenance chip, and a "Download" link. A content review then runs automatically. The result notice opens with "Health Canada review:" followed by either "no blocking content gaps." or a count such as "2 to fix, 1 to check.", then a list of findings — each with a severity mark, message, a suggested edit line, and an "HC guidance ↗" link. You can edit fields and press "Review vs Health Canada" again before moving on; the right-rail gate flags and progress bar update as sections complete.
